context: A uni intern interviews a manager about strategy
purpose: Teach: 原案/本業/都度/縛ら/検事/集客/文言/網羅

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 集客戦略、本業との関係、どうバランスしてますか。
lines.en: How do you balance customer acquisition strategy with your core business?
lines.style: Careful, genuinely curious. Lean forward slightly. Respectful pace—not rushed. Soft attack on the opening, building into the question with real interest.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 原案レベルから網羅的に分析しています。
lines.en: We analyze it comprehensively from the very first draft stage.
lines.style: Clear and steady. Competent without being proud. A direct answer delivered with quiet confidence. Even pacing, grounded.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 文言の更新、都度行われるんですか。
lines.en: So the wording gets revised each time?
lines.style: Probing further, but gently. Slight lift at the end—genuine question, not challenging. Leaning in to understand the detail.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: はい。法務、元検事の助言を反映し、契約に縛られない形を作ります。
lines.en: Yes. We incorporate advice from our legal team and an ex-prosecutor, so we build it to avoid binding contracts.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact explanation with subtle emphasis on the rigour. Measured pace. Professional warmth—she's explaining something important and wants him to understand.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 参考になりました、ありがとうございます。
lines.style: Genuine gratitude. Warm closing. Soft landing—not abrupt. The relief of someone who got what they came for.
